threads.title: Peter Beyls
threads.note: A new pioneer, opened 2026-10-06. For more than fifty years Beyls has moved between electronic music, computer drawing, artificial intelligence, instrument building, robotics and painting — the machines changed radically, the questions stayed remarkably persistent. A thread held open to build a Beyls perspective: his span touches the Thinking Machine, the Sonic Dimension, and Another Dimension, and his 1968-onward practice poses Mechanical Reverie's own criteria-partnership question — what does the machine value, and who decides.

members.why: 'Flora' — his generative stroke-field: a dense swarm of short directional colored marks accumulating into a vibrating field. The first Beyls piece, and the archive's return to saturated colour on white.

threads.title: Computed Space & Instrument Imaging
threads.note: NASA and aerospace graphics that render what an instrument or a trajectory would see — the computed view, checked against the real sky or the real terrain. Held at two, both Alfred Lunde's. A third appeared on 2026-10-05 (Sue C. Wynn's Apollo 16 traverse-briefing panorama — 'full panoramas of what they will see standing on the surface') but was not made. Graduates to a room if the computed view recurs.

members.why: 'By God, There It Is' — NASA's VIEW program (Lunde, 1968) computing the sun's sighting through Apollo 13's fogged optics; the render verified against the real sky.
'Already Begun' — Lunde's 1985 computer drawing of the large space station, the same engineer's imaging carried into architecture.
